chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'I enter the mosque and find the Imam has already bowed, and the people have bowed, so I cannot call the adhan, establish the iqamah, and say the takbir.' He said to me, 'If that is the case, then enter with them in the bowing and count it as one, for it is among the best of your bowings.'
Isḥāq said, 'When I heard the adhan for Maghrib while I was sitting at my door, I said to the servant,
See if the prayer has been established.

He came to me and said, 'Yes.' So I rose quickly and entered the mosque, and I found the people had bowed. I bowed with the first row I caught and counted it. Then after departing, I prayed four rak'at.

Then I turned away, and behold, five or six of my neighbors from the Makhzūmīs and the Umayyīs had come up to me, seated me, and said, 'O Abū Hāshim, may Allah reward you well for yourself. By Allah, we saw the opposite of what we thought of you and what was said about you.'

I said, 'What is that?' They said, 'We followed you when you rose for the prayer, and we thought you did not follow the prayer with us. We found that you had counted the prayer with us and prayed with our prayer. May Allah be pleased with you and reward you well.'
He said, 'So I said to them, 'Glory be to Allah, is this said for someone like me?'
He said, 'So I knew that Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) did not command me except while fearing for me this and the like of it.'

And whenever the follower finishes his recitation before the Imam finishes, he should glorify Allah (Exalted is He) or leave a verse from his surah until the Imam finishes his recitation, then complete it. Whatever he does, it is sufficient for him.

key_terms.أُؤَذِّنَ وَأُقِيمَ: To call adhan and establish iqamah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a latecomer who joins the Imam in ruku' without adhan and iqamah, and how should he handle finishing his recitation before the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence regarding congregational prayer, emphasizing that joining the Imam in ruku' suffices for validity even without the full adhan and iqamah. The narrative underscores the social dimension of fiqh, showing how strict adherence to ritual norms can prevent unnecessary criticism (ghibah or takfir) from the community. It concludes with a specific ruling for the follower (ma'mum) who finishes recitation early, instructing him to either glorify Allah or pause with a verse until the Imam completes his recitation, ensuring synchronization and validity.
